issue.title: Gate cipher_memory_security to desktop platforms only (disable on Android + iOS)
issue.body:
## Summary

Disable SQLCipher's `cipher_memory_security` on mobile targets (`android`, `ios`) and keep it enabled on desktop targets (`macos`, `linux`, `windows`). On Android the feature emits hundreds of error lines per session for a defense that **structurally cannot run** in the app sandbox; on iOS there is no on-disk swap for app processes for it to defend against. On desktop platforms it remains a useful defense-in-depth and should stay on.

## Symptom

A user logcat from `org.parres.whitenoise:2024` (Android 16, Pixel `caiman`) captured during a routine session shows **422 occurrences** of:

```
05-08 15:55:05.859 D sqlcipher: ERROR MEMORY sqlcipher_mlock: mlock() returned -1 errno=12
05-08 15:55:05.860 D sqlcipher: ERROR MEMORY sqlcipher_mlock: mlock() returned -1 errno=12
05-08 15:55:05.860 D sqlcipher: ERROR MEMORY sqlcipher_mlock: mlock() returned -1 errno=12
... (419 more) ...
```

`errno=12` is `ENOMEM`. SQLCipher's memory-security feature attempts to `mlock(2)` decrypted page memory so it can't be paged to swap. On Android:

- Unprivileged apps lack `CAP_IPC_LOCK` and therefore cannot `mlock` outside `RLIMIT_MEMLOCK`.
- `RLIMIT_MEMLOCK` is **64 KB** for app processes by default — exhausted by the first SQLCipher page.
- Every subsequent `mlock` call returns `ENOMEM`. SQLCipher logs the failure and continues (the operation is best-effort), so the database itself works fine.
- The result is hundreds of \"ERROR MEMORY\" log lines per session for a feature that is doing nothing.

## Why disable on Android (and iOS), keep on desktop

`cipher_memory_security` does two things:
1. `mlock()` decrypted SQLite page memory → prevents pages going to swap.
2. Zero memory before `free()` → in-process hardening against use-after-free disclosure.

Part (2) is platform-agnostic and cheap; not in scope for this issue (and we're not changing it — disabling the PRAGMA disables the whole feature, but the security cost of losing (2) is small relative to the size of our threat model). The contested piece is (1).

(1) defends against a specific threat: an attacker recovering decrypted database pages from the **swap medium** via offline forensic access. Whether that threat exists is a per-platform question:

| Platform | `mlock` callable? | On-disk swap for app processes? | Swap encrypted by default? | Memory-security useful? | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Android** | ❌ No (RLIMIT_MEMLOCK=64KB, no `CAP_IPC_LOCK`) | No — `zram` (compressed in RAM, never disk) | n/a | No — feature literally cannot run | **OFF** |
| **iOS** | ✅ Yes | No — compressed memory + jetsam, no on-disk swap for app processes | n/a | No — nothing to lock against | **OFF** |
| **macOS** | ✅ (subject to limits) | Yes — `/private/var/vm/swapfile*` | Yes when FileVault is on | Modest defense, real defense without FileVault | **ON** |
| **Linux** | ✅ (cap/limit dependent) | Often — and frequently unencrypted (LUKS commonly only covers `/`, not swap) | Often **NOT** | Yes — strongest case | **ON** |
| **Windows** | ✅ via `VirtualLock` | Yes — `pagefile.sys` | Only on BitLocker volumes | Yes | **ON** |

iOS deserves a brief callout because it's the non-obvious one: iOS app processes do not get on-disk swap. Memory pressure causes either compression (in-RAM, never disk) or jetsam termination. There is no swap medium for `mlock` to defend the database pages from. Leaving the feature on isn't *harmful* on iOS (no log spam — `mlock` succeeds), but it's not buying defense-in-depth either. We're choosing the honest policy: OFF where the threat doesn't exist, ON where it does.

This matches what other privacy-focused apps (Signal, ProtonMail, etc.) do with SQLCipher on Android, and it matches Zetetic's own guidance that memory security is \"not effective on Android.\"

## Patch

The cipher PRAGMAs are already declared via `.pragma(...)` on `SqliteConnectOptions` in `src/whitenoise/database/encryption.rs::encrypted_connect_options` (lines 376–388). Add a `cfg`-gated shadowing `let` after the chain:

```rust
pub(super) fn encrypted_connect_options(
    db_path: &Path,
    config: &EncryptionConfig,
    create: bool,
) -> SqliteConnectOptions {
    let opts = SqliteConnectOptions::new()
        .filename(db_path)
        .create_if_missing(create)
        .pragma(\"key\", key_pragma_value(config))
        .pragma(\"cipher_compatibility\", \"4\")
        .pragma(\"temp_store\", \"MEMORY\")
        .busy_timeout(Duration::from_millis(u64::from(super::DB_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS)));

    // SQLCipher's memory-security feature mlock()s decrypted page memory to
    // keep it out of swap. This defense is only meaningful on platforms with
    // on-disk swap that may be unencrypted at rest:
    //   - Android: app sandbox blocks mlock entirely (RLIMIT_MEMLOCK=64KB,
    //     no CAP_IPC_LOCK). The feature emits hundreds of ENOMEM log lines
    //     per session and does nothing.
    //   - iOS: app processes have no on-disk swap (compressed memory + jetsam).
    //     Nothing to lock against.
    // On macOS, Linux, and Windows the feature provides genuine
    // defense-in-depth and remains enabled.
    #[cfg(any(target_os = \"android\", target_os = \"ios\"))]
    let opts = opts.pragma(\"cipher_memory_security\", \"OFF\");

    opts
}
```

Notes:
- `#[cfg(any(target_os = \"android\", target_os = \"ios\"))]` on the shadowing `let` is compile-time gated — the line is literally absent from desktop binaries. Zero runtime cost.
- `.pragma(...)` is the right mechanism here because sqlx applies these to the connection at open time, before any data access. `cipher_memory_security` must be set before page operations; this guarantees that ordering.
- The unencrypted-connection path (`unencrypted_connect_options`, lines 367–374) is unaffected — there are no decrypted pages to lock there.

## Verification plan

**On Android (the primary motivation):**
1. Build and install. Run a session that exercises the database (login, view groups, send a message).
2. `adb logcat | grep sqlcipher` — should show **zero** `mlock() returned -1` lines.
3. Confirm app behavior is otherwise identical (login, message send/receive, group ops).

**On iOS:**
1. Build and install. Same exercise.
2. No observable change expected (mlock was succeeding silently before; now it's not called at all). Slightly faster connection open due to fewer syscalls.

**On desktop (macOS dev machine + CI Linux):**
1. Run the existing test suite — `cargo test -p whitenoise --tests`.
2. Confirm no behavioral regression. The `cfg` gating means desktop binaries are byte-equivalent to today aside from optimization variance.

A regression test could assert that the PRAGMA chain on Android targets includes `cipher_memory_security = OFF` and on desktop targets it does not, gated with the same `cfg`. Optional — the patch is small enough that visual review is sufficient.

## Out of scope

- The `unencrypted_connect_options` code path (no encryption → no decrypted pages → memory security irrelevant).
- Changing other cipher settings (`cipher_compatibility`, `temp_store`).
- Compile-time-stripping the SQLCipher memory-security feature via custom build flags. Disabling at runtime via PRAGMA achieves the same outcome without forking the build.

## References

- `src/whitenoise/database/encryption.rs:376–388` — `encrypted_connect_options`
- SQLCipher docs on `cipher_memory_security`: https://www.zetetic.net/sqlcipher/sqlcipher-api/#cipher_memory_security
- Same user logcat that surfaced this also surfaced #813 (`add_members` post-publish-failure stuck state) and parres-hq/whitenoise-flutter equivalent #645 (`WnSystemNotice` timer crash).

issue.title: add_members retry hits 'Duplicate signature key in proposals and group' after a publish failure
issue.body:
## Symptom

A user reports intermittent failures inviting/adding members to groups. A logcat from the Flutter client (`whitenoise` app, whitenoise-rs `0.2.1` @ `8e7052f`) captures the failure mode in 20 seconds:

```
15:55:16.093  SEVERE: AddToGroupScreen: Failed to add user to group:
              ApiError.whitenoise(message: Nostr manager error: No relay accepted the event)
15:55:22.318  SEVERE: AddToGroupScreen: Failed to add user to group:
              ApiError.whitenoise(message: MDK error: Duplicate signature key in proposals and group.)
15:55:36.234  SEVERE: AddToGroupScreen: Failed to add user to group:
              ApiError.whitenoise(message: MDK error: Duplicate signature key in proposals and group.)
```

First attempt: relay publish failed. Subsequent retries against the same target: `DuplicateSignatureKeyValue` from openmls. The user perceives this as \"sometimes invites work, often they don't\" — but it's actually two regimes: a normal happy path, and a sticky error state entered whenever the first publish fails ambiguously.

## Why the existing rollback isn't enough

`groups/publish.rs::publish_and_merge_commit` already does the right thing for the \"clean failure\" case: on publish error it calls `mdk.clear_pending_commit(group_id)` to roll back the pending commit before returning. This was the fix for #623 and is verified by `test_add_members_no_merge_on_publish_failure` and `test_publish_and_merge_commit_rollback_on_publish_failure`.

The gap is that `publish_event_with_retry` returning `Err` is **not the same as \"nothing was published\"**:

1. A relay can accept the event and persist it but fail to return `OK` within the retry window (lossy connection, slow relay, OK ack dropped).
2. A subset of relays may accept while the aggregate retry policy still resolves to error.
3. The client's own subscription on the group's relay set will then **receive its own evolution event back** and the event processor will merge it into local MLS state — advancing the group past the point we just rolled back locally.

Once that happens, the next `add_members` call for the same target hits openmls's `ProposalValidationError::DuplicateSignatureKeyValue` because the target is now genuinely a member of the group (locally and on the wire), but the UI's last signal was an error and the user retries blindly.

So the bug isn't \"rollback is missing\" — it's \"rollback is racing the event-processor's ingest of our own published event, and the publish-failure error is ambiguous about which side won.\"

## Hardening ideas

A few non-exclusive directions, ordered by surface area:

### 1. Disambiguate `publish_event_with_retry` failure modes

Today the caller sees \"No relay accepted the event\" — a single string. Distinguish:
- **`PublishFailed::NoRelayAccepted`** — every attempted relay rejected or timed out without ack. Safe to roll back.
- **`PublishFailed::Inconclusive`** — at least one relay was contacted but we couldn't confirm acceptance (timeout, dropped OK, partial success below threshold). Treat as \"may have landed\" — caller should reconcile, not blindly roll back, and definitely not blindly retry the same MLS operation.

This is the highest-leverage change: it lets `publish_and_merge_commit` make a correct decision instead of always clearing the pending commit and returning the same error string.

### 2. Reconcile-then-decide on inconclusive publish

When a publish is inconclusive, before rolling back:
- Wait briefly for the local event processor to drain (we may already be ingesting our own event via subscription).
- Re-fetch group state / pending proposals and check whether the evolution event's epoch was applied.
- If applied → don't roll back, treat the operation as successful, surface a `RelayAckTimeout` warning instead of an error.
- If not applied within the window → roll back as today.

### 3. Idempotent retry semantics for `add_members_to_group`

Currently a retry by the caller starts from scratch and re-runs `mdk.add_members(...)`. Make the API itself robust: pre-flight check whether each requested member is already in the group (post any in-flight ingest) and short-circuit those cases with a structured `AlreadyMember { pubkey }` warning rather than letting the error surface as the openmls duplicate-signature-key failure.

This is also the right place to handle the case where the user's own event has already been merged from subscription: the caller asks \"add Alice,\" we discover Alice is already a member, return Ok with a `nothing_to_do` flag (or `MemberAlreadyPresent` typed result) — the UI shows success instead of an error.

### 4. Map `DuplicateSignatureKeyValue` in `map_mdk_add_members_error`

Today `map_mdk_add_members_error` only specializes `InviteeMissingRequiredProposal`. The duplicate-signature path falls through to `WhitenoiseError::from(other)`, which is what produces the raw \"Duplicate signature key in proposals and group.\" string the user sees. Even without (1)-(3), translate this into a typed `WhitenoiseError::MemberAlreadyInGroup { member_pubkey: Option<PublicKey> }` so callers and clients can react meaningfully (refresh group state, dismiss the screen with success, etc.) rather than treating it as a generic MDK failure.

## UI-layer requirement (cross-cutting)

The Flutter client surfaces these as `ApiError.whitenoise(message: ...)` raw strings. To give users actionable feedback, the Rust API must expose **structured, exhaustive error variants** that the client can switch on, not stringly-typed messages. Concretely, the variants the UI needs to distinguish for the add-member flow are at minimum:

- `RelayPublishFailed { retryable: bool }` — \"check connection, try again\"
- `RelayPublishInconclusive` — \"we're not sure if it went through; refreshing…\" (and the UI should refresh group state, not retry)
- `MemberAlreadyInGroup { pubkey }` — \"this user is already in the group\" (silent success / dismiss)
- `MemberKeyPackageUnavailable { pubkey }` — \"this user hasn't published a key package\"
- `GroupRejectedMember { ... }` — already exists, good

Without these, the client cannot do better than show a toast with a raw string, and the user re-enters the failure loop.

## Repro

Hard to reproduce deterministically because it depends on a relay returning ambiguous ack behavior, but the following should hit it reliably:

1. Configure the user's account with a single group relay that accepts `EVENT` but is patched to drop `OK` responses (or use a relay with very high latency near the retry threshold).
2. Attempt `add_members_to_group` for a target user with a valid published key package.
3. Observe `publish_event_with_retry` returns `Err`, `clear_pending_commit` runs.
4. Wait ~5 s for the client's own subscription to ingest the published event.
5. Retry the same `add_members_to_group` call → hits `DuplicateSignatureKeyValue`.

## Related

- #623 — the original publish-before-merge ordering work; this is a follow-on edge case the existing fix doesn't cover.
- #503 — retry logic for publish failures; relevant context for the retry policy that produces the inconclusive case.

## Environment

- App: `org.parres.whitenoise:2024` (Android)
- Device: Pixel `caiman` / Android 16 (`BP4A.260205.002/2026050701`)
- whitenoise-rs: `0.2.1` @ `8e7052fecbb0f846d697304df8a2492ab51a9a4c`
- Captured: 2026-05-08 15:55 UTC

Logs and full Flutter stack available on request.

issue.title: Merge master into arch-refactor (post mute_list per-account)
issue.body:
## Summary

Catches `arch-refactor` up with `master`. Two merge cycles: the first absorbs the master PRs that were waiting after #810 (mute_list per-account), the second picks up two more PRs that landed on master while we were resolving conflicts.

## Master PRs absorbed

**First cycle** (commit `75c09c6`):
- #802 — `feat(whitenoise/chat_list): expose get_chat_list_item public method`
- #804 — `Make chat-list unread badges ignore blocked authors`
- #805 — `feat(cli wnd): add --discovery-relays flag to wnd`
- #807 — `Add CODEOWNERS default reviewers`

**Second cycle** (commit `0a1af52`):
- #808 — `Feat/add group state streaming` (new module + integration scenario)
- #811 — `Recover external signer subscriptions after registration`

## Commits

- `75c09c6` — first-cycle merge
- `14cdca7` — narrow the API surface introduced by the merge: keep `build_chat_list_item` `pub(crate)` and add a public `pub deprecated fn get_chat_list_item` wrapper instead; revert the temporary `test_utils` visibility/gate widening
- `0a1af52` — second-cycle merge
- `634d839` — fix two integration scenarios that broke under the merge: port master's deletion-author plumbing on top of arch-refactor's per-account scope, and fix `process_and_emit_outgoing_message` to pass the shared DB (not the per-account DB) to `MediaFile::find_by_group`

## Adapting master's content to arch-refactor

Master targets the pre-arch-refactor world (single shared DB, no session pattern). Five changes were needed on top of the conflict resolutions:

1. **`count_visible_unread_for_group(s)` SQL referenced `ml.account_pubkey`**, a column dropped by m0042 when `mute_list` moved per-account. Dropped the clause; kept the `Option<&PublicKey>` parameter as a feature toggle.
2. **PR #804's `count_visible_unread_for_group(s)` had zero callers in arch-refactor** after the merge. Flipped both call sites (`session/chat_list.rs:250`, `chat_list.rs:367`) to the visible variants so the blocked-author filter actually fires.
3. **PR #802's `GetChatListItem` enum variant + dispatch arm + roundtrip test** never made it into the extracted `crates/whitenoise-cli` location. Ported.
4. **`crates/whitenoise-cli/src/cli/dispatch.rs:tests` had a stale `crate::whitenoise::test_utils::*` import** from before the cli was extracted to its own crate. Removed the heavy test it gated (its JSON-shape coverage is duplicated by the protocol roundtrip test).
5. **Two `db_migrations/*.sql` files** master added to a folder arch-refactor deleted in PR #783 (Rust migrations rework) silently re-appeared via the merge. Removed.

## Cycle 2 wiring

#808's group-state-streaming feature lands the new `whitenoise::group_state_streaming` module and depends on a `GroupStateStreamManager` field on `Whitenoise`. Threaded the field into `SharedServices` (matching the existing pattern for the other stream managers) and wired the `LeftGroup` / `RemovedFromGroup` emissions into `session::membership::mark_as_left/removed`. Without that wiring the feature would have shipped dormant.

#811's external-signer recovery uses `effective_inbox_relays` for nip65 fallback. Kept master's intent; rewrote the new tests to use arch-refactor's `whitenoise.shared.*` accessors and `session.deactivate_subscriptions()` (master's `relay_control.deactivate_account_subscriptions(...)` has no arch-refactor equivalent).

## Integration test fixes (commit `634d839`)

Two integration scenarios broke during the merge and are fixed in this PR:

1. **`AdvancedMessagingScenario::verify_reaction_deletion`** — master added deletion-author plumbing in earlier commits that wasn't ported to arch-refactor's per-account scope. Threaded `deletion.pubkey` through `cache_deletion → apply_deletions_to_targets → apply_single_deletion`; reaction and message branches now gate on `&target.author == deletion_author`; `mark_deleted` takes `target_author: &PublicKey` and adds `AND author = ?` to the SQL; `find_orphaned_deletions` returns `Vec<AggregatedMessage>` so the orphaned-deletion application path can author-check before applying. Updated 11 test call sites and the outgoing-deletion path in `session/messages.rs`. Scenario passes 14/14.
2. **`ChatMediaUploadScenario::SendMessageWithMediaTestCase`** — `no such table: media_blobs`. Latent bug from PR #789 (`media_references` move): `process_and_emit_outgoing_message` was passing `self.db()` (per-account `Database`) where `MediaFile::find_by_group` expects `shared_db`. Swapped to `&self.session.shared.database`. Scenario passes 11/11.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo check --workspace --tests --all-features` clean
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` clean
- [x] `just precommit-quick` clean
- [x] `just int-test advanced-messaging` — 14/14
- [x] `just int-test chat-media-upload` — 11/11

## Master PRs absorbed

**First cycle** (commit `75c09c6`):
- #802 — `feat(whitenoise/chat_list): expose get_chat_list_item public method`
- #804 — `Make chat-list unread badges ignore blocked authors`
- #805 — `feat(cli wnd): add --discovery-relays flag to wnd`
- #807 — `Add CODEOWNERS default reviewers`

**Second cycle** (commit `0a1af52`):
- #808 — `Feat/add group state streaming` (new module + integration scenario)
- #811 — `Recover external signer subscriptions after registration`

## Commits

- `75c09c6` — first-cycle merge
- `14cdca7` — narrow the API surface introduced by the merge: keep `build_chat_list_item` `pub(crate)` and add a public `pub deprecated fn get_chat_list_item` wrapper instead; revert the temporary `test_utils` visibility/gate widening
- `0a1af52` — second-cycle merge
- `634d839` — fix two integration scenarios that broke under the merge: port master's deletion-author plumbing on top of arch-refactor's per-account scope, and fix `process_and_emit_outgoing_message` to pass the shared DB (not the per-account DB) to `MediaFile::find_by_group`

## Adapting master's content to arch-refactor

Master targets the pre-arch-refactor world (single shared DB, no session pattern). Five changes were needed on top of the conflict resolutions:

1. **`count_visible_unread_for_group(s)` SQL referenced `ml.account_pubkey`**, a column dropped by m0042 when `mute_list` moved per-account. Dropped the clause; kept the `Option<&PublicKey>` parameter as a feature toggle.
2. **PR #804's `count_visible_unread_for_group(s)` had zero callers in arch-refactor** after the merge. Flipped both call sites (`session/chat_list.rs:250`, `chat_list.rs:367`) to the visible variants so the blocked-author filter actually fires.
3. **PR #802's `GetChatListItem` enum variant + dispatch arm + roundtrip test** never made it into the extracted `crates/whitenoise-cli` location. Ported.
4. **`crates/whitenoise-cli/src/cli/dispatch.rs:tests` had a stale `crate::whitenoise::test_utils::*` import** from before the cli was extracted to its own crate. Removed the heavy test it gated (its JSON-shape coverage is duplicated by the protocol roundtrip test).
5. **Two `db_migrations/*.sql` files** master added to a folder arch-refactor deleted in PR #783 (Rust migrations rework) silently re-appeared via the merge. Removed.

#808's group-state-streaming feature lands the new `whitenoise::group_state_streaming` module and depends on a `GroupStateStreamManager` field on `Whitenoise`. - [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` clean
- [x] `just precommit-quick` clean

- [x] Gather context from PR description and changed files
- [x] Review core logic changes (aggregated_messages, group_state_streaming)
- [x] Review arch-refactor adaptations (session/, shared.rs)
- [x] Review CLI changes
- [x] Review integration test additions
- [x] Post final review

---

This is a well-executed merge with thorough documentation in the PR body. The adaptations required to make master's content work on arch-refactor are all addressed and explained. Below are findings by area.

---

### `group_state_streaming` — New Module

**Overall: solid.** The design correctly mirrors `MessageStreamManager` and the per-`(account, group)` keying is the right call.

**`manager.rs`:** The cleanup path in `emit` is correct. The sequence `drop(sender)` → `remove_if(|_, s| s.receiver_count() == 0)` closes the TOCTOU window: if a new subscriber races in between the failed send and the `remove_if`, the predicate will be false and the entry is preserved. Good.

**One minor observation** (`streaming.rs:161-181`): `subscribe_to_group_state` correctly validates the `AccountGroup` row before subscribing to prevent orphaned sender entries. However, unlike `subscribe_to_group_messages`, there is no drain loop. The doc explains this is intentional ("real-time only — transitions, not persistent state"), but this means a `LeftGroup` event emitted in the narrow window between group validation and the subscribe call would be silently lost. This is likely acceptable for the use case, but is worth a brief note in the doc-comment. [Fix this →](https://claude.ai/code?q=Add%20a%20note%20to%20the%20subscribe_to_group_state%20doc-comment%20in%20src%2Fwhitenoise%2Fstreaming.rs%20around%20line%20161%20clarifying%20that%20events%20emitted%20in%20the%20gap%20between%20AccountGroup%20validation%20and%20the%20subscribe%20call%20may%20be%20missed%2C%20and%20that%20this%20is%20acceptable%20because%20group%20state%20changes%20are%20typically%20followed%20by%20navigation%20away%20from%20the%20chat%20view.&repo=marmot-protocol/whitenoise-rs)

---

### Deletion-Author Plumbing

**Security improvement.** The combination of:
1. Application-level author check in `apply_single_deletion` (`handle_mls_message.rs:785`, `819`)
2. SQL-level guard added to `mark_deleted`: `AND author = ?` (`aggregated_messages.rs:1049`)
3. Orphaned-deletion author check in `apply_orphaned_reactions_and_deletions` (`handle_mls_message.rs:974`)

...provides proper double protection against a malicious peer attempting to wipe another member's messages via a crafted kind-5 event. Belt and suspenders is appropriate here.

**`find_orphaned_deletions` return type change** (from `Vec<EventId>` to `Vec<AggregatedMessage>`) was necessary to give the orphan path access to `deletion.author` for the author check. Correct.

---

### Mute-List Unread Count (`count_unread_for_group_filtered`)

The `account_pubkey` parameter has been repurposed as a feature toggle: `Some` means "filter blocked authors," `None` means "no filter." The SQL at line 1394–1399 no longer joins on `ml.account_pubkey` because the mute_list now lives in the per-account DB (migration m0042), so the database connection itself provides implicit account scoping.

This is correct **as long as** the function is always called with the per-account `Database`. Looking at the two call sites confirmed by the PR:
- `session/chat_list.rs:250` — uses the session's account DB ✓
- `chat_list.rs:384` — uses `session.account_db.inner` ✓

**`count_visible_unread_for_groups` batch variant** (`aggregated_messages.rs:1425`): the same pattern applies. The function takes a single `&Database` for all groups, which is fine as long as all groups belong to the same account — which is always the case since the callers iterate over a single account's groups.

---

### `process_and_emit_outgoing_message` DB Routing Fix

`session/messages.rs:384-388` now correctly passes `&self.session.shared.database` instead of `self.session.account_db.inner.pool` to `MediaFile::find_by_group`. This is the right fix: `media_blobs` lives in the shared DB, not the per-account DB. The fix is minimal and targeted.

---

### `register_external_signer` Subscription Recovery (`signer.rs`)

The new recovery flow at lines 61–91 uses `effective_inbox_relays` for NIP-65 fallback, matching master's intent. The `ensure_global_subscriptions()` best-effort call is correct defensive programming for the startup-gap case.

---

### `build_chat_list_item` Divergence

The comment at `chat_list.rs:284-293` correctly documents the known divergence between the Whitenoise-level path (MDK group membership for DM peer lookup) and `ChatListOps::build_item` (batch SQL). This is tracked for phase 15 removal. The comment is clear and the deprecated marker is appropriate.

---

### CLI Changes

The `dispatch.rs` test cleanup (removing the stale `crate::whitenoise::test_utils::*` import and the heavy JSON-shape test) is correct. The protocol roundtrip test in `protocol.rs` covers the shape adequately. The `GetChatListItem` dispatch arm port is clean.

---

### Integration Tests

`GroupStateStreamingScenario` is well-structured: separate MLS groups per phase prevents membership races. Phase 4 (stream isolation) correctly awaits the positive event first to synchronise on MLS propagation before asserting the admin's stream remained silent. Good.

`VerifyNoGroupStateUpdateTestCase` using a short timeout to assert silence is a standard pattern and works here since the positive event (phase 4) is verified first before asserting silence, ensuring MLS propagation has completed.

---

### Minor Issues

1. **`chat_list.rs:597` `#[allow(deprecated)]`** — The `resolve_group_image_paths` method is not deprecated itself but calls `resolve_group_image_path` which may be. The allow attribute suppresses any chain warnings. No action needed, just noting it's intentional.

2. **`streaming.rs:273`** — `tracing::warn!("subscription drain lagged by {n} messages")` lacks a `target:` field, inconsistent with other warn calls in the same file. [Fix this →](https://claude.ai/code?q=In%20src%2Fwhitenoise%2Fstreaming.rs%2C%20the%20tracing%3A%3Awarn%21%20calls%20at%20around%20lines%20273%20and%20330%20are%20missing%20the%20target%3A%20field.%20Add%20target%3A%20%22whitenoise%3A%3Astreaming%22%20to%20them%20to%20be%20consistent%20with%20other%20log%20calls%20in%20the%20codebase.&repo=marmot-protocol/whitenoise-rs)

---

### Summary

The merge is technically sound. The four arch-refactor adaptations (mute_list SQL fix, dormant-feature activation for `count_visible_unread`, CLI port, stale import removal) are all correct. The two integration scenario fixes (deletion-author plumbing, shared-DB routing) address real bugs with minimal, targeted changes. The new `GroupStateStreamingScenario` properly validates end-to-end isolation.

Issues found are minor: one design note about the no-drain window in `subscribe_to_group_state`, and one style inconsistency with a missing `target:` on two `tracing::warn!` calls.

> The `None` branch defaults `is_private = true` for the rollback and logs a
> debug-level message. The PR description describes this as "the safer choice
> for a rollback." That is correct in isolation, but if the entry genuinely
> vanished (concurrent sync wiped it), the subsequent `delete` will silently
> succeed against a non-existent row, and then `publish_mute_list` will publish
> a list that no longer includes the target — which is arguably the right
> outcome. However, the `is_private = true` default is only meaningful for the
> rollback `insert`, and a rollback `insert` on a row that was already removed
> by a concurrent sync would *re-add* that row.
> 
> The rollback path (`MuteListEntry::insert(target_pubkey, is_private, ...)`)
> uses `INSERT OR IGNORE`, so the concrete risk is: concurrent sync deletes the
> row → `find_by_muted_pubkey` returns `None` → `delete` is a no-op → publish
> fails → rollback `insert OR IGNORE` re-inserts the row (since it no longer
> exists). The user ends up still blocked when they should not be.
> 
> This is an edge case, but the `None` branch silently makes the wrong
> decision. A `debug!` log alone is insufficient — at minimum a `warn!` should
> fire because the caller needs to know a logical inconsistency occurred. More
> robustly: if `find_by_muted_pubkey` returns `None`, skip the delete and the
> publish (the user is already not in the local list), and return `Ok(())`.

> `INSERT OR IGNORE` returns `rows_affected() == 0` for *both* a CHECK-constraint
> violation (malformed pubkey) *and* a UNIQUE conflict (duplicate row). In the
> context of a fresh per-account table that starts empty, a UNIQUE conflict can
> only happen if the migration runs twice (idempotency path). Today the warning
> message says "constraint violation — likely malformed muted\_pubkey", which
> would be misleading if the actual cause is a UNIQUE collision from a re-run.
> 
> The comment in the code notes this ambiguity ("CHECK / UNIQUE constraint
> failures get swallowed"), but the warning text presented to operators doesn't
> reflect it. Either:
> 
> - Split the insert query into a prior `SELECT EXISTS(...)` check so the two
>   cases can be distinguished, or
> - Update the warning message to name both possible causes so an operator
>   reading the log is not misled into thinking their data is corrupt when it
>   is actually a harmless re-run.
>

issue.title: feat: move mute_list to per-account database (m0042 + m0043)
issue.body:
## Summary

Moves the `mute_list` table from the shared SQLite database into each account's per-account DB file, then drops the now-empty shared table. This is the last bit of per-account state that hadn't migrated yet, and it's blocking a clean re-merge of master.

## Why now

Master's PR #804 (`feat: ignore blocked authors in unread badges`) added a `count_visible_unread_for_group` query that joins `aggregated_messages` (per-account post-Phase 18d) with `mute_list` (shared). That cross-DB subquery can't run on arch-refactor — it fails with `no such table: mute_list` against the per-account pool.

Rather than bridge with `ATTACH DATABASE`, this moves the table to where it logically belongs. After this lands, the next master merge brings master's signature changes through cleanly because both tables now live in the same DB.

## What changed

**Migrations**

- `m0042_move_mute_list` (LocalMigration, v42) creates per-account `mute_list` and copies rows from shared filtered to the owning account. Per-row `rows_affected()` accounting emits `tracing::warn!` on any silently-skipped constraint violations so corrupt source rows leave a diagnostic trail.
- `m0043_drop_shared_mute_list` (GlobalMigration, v43) drops the shared table and its account-scoped index. Runs after every account has completed v42, in the same boot.
- `account_pubkey` column dropped — redundant once the table is per-account. UNIQUE collapses from `(account_pubkey, muted_pubkey)` to `muted_pubkey`.
- Schema baked into `fresh_account_schema.sql` so future bootstrap rebaselines pick it up.

**DAO (`database/mute_list.rs`)**

- `MuteListEntry` no longer carries `account_pubkey`.
- All methods take `&AccountDatabase` instead of `&Database` and drop the `account_pubkey` parameter.
- `find_by_account` → `find_all`; `find_by_account_and_target` → `find_by_muted_pubkey` (matches column-name suffix convention used across other DAOs).
- `exists()` uses `SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 ...)` for short-circuit boolean semantics.

**Session (`session/mute_list.rs`)**

- `db()` returns `&AccountDatabase`.
- `account_relay_urls()` reaches into `&shared.database` directly for `Account` / `User` / `Relay` reads (those tables stay shared).
- `unblock_user` rollback path: explicit `match` with `tracing::debug!` when the entry vanishes between exists-check and read, instead of a silent `unwrap_or(true)`.

**Docs**

- `AccountDatabase` doc comment now lists `mute_list` alongside the other per-account tables.

## Migration safety

- Existing accounts: rows copy from `shared.mute_list WHERE account_pubkey = ?` into the per-account file before v43 drops shared.
- Fresh accounts: bootstrap creates the table from `fresh_account_schema.sql`; m0042's `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` is a no-op; data copy hits empty shared; m0043 drops the empty shared table.
- Idempotency: each migration runs in its own transaction; `INSERT OR IGNORE` makes re-runs safe; `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS` is idempotent.
- Corrupt source rows (CHECK violations on hex format) are silently skipped rather than aborting startup — a `tracing::warn!` records the count, and `migration_silently_skips_invalid_pubkey_rows` test pins this contract.
- Ordering across kinds: the migrator processes a unified version timeline, so all per-account v42 instances complete before the v43 global drop runs.

## Downstream impact

`MuteListEntry` is publicly re-exported via `lib.rs:72`. The `marmot-protocol/whitenoise` Flutter app's bridge layer at `whitenoise/rust/src/api/mute_list.rs` reads `e.account_pubkey.to_hex()` (line 20) plus a unit test that constructs the struct directly. The released app pins whitenoise-rs by git rev so it isn't retroactively broken — but the next rev bump on the Flutter side requires:

- Drop `account_pubkey: String` field from the bridge `MuteListEntry` struct
- Drop `account_pubkey: e.account_pubkey.to_hex()` from the `From` impl
- Update the `WhitenoiseEntry { ... }` literals in the two unit tests
- Run `flutter_rust_bridge_codegen generate` + `dart run build_runner build`

No Dart consumers of `accountPubkey` exist outside the auto-generated bridge code, so the Flutter app side is ~8 lines of Rust + a regen.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Companion PR on `marmot-protocol/whitenoise` that lands together with the eventual arch-refactor → master merge (drops `account_pubkey` from the bridge struct, regen).

## Test plan

- [x] `just precommit-quick` passes — fmt, docs, clippy, dead_code, all unit tests
- [x] m0042 tests: account-scoped copy, empty source, missing shared table, silent skip on invalid hex
- [x] m0043 tests: drops table when present, idempotent when absent
- [x] DAO tests: insert/exists/delete/find_all/find_by_muted_pubkey/sync_from_event with the new schema
- [x] Session tests: block/unblock/sync_and_emit go through the per-account DB

issue.title: feat: move mute_list to per-account database (m0042 + m0043)
issue.body:
## Summary

Moves the `mute_list` table from the shared SQLite database into each account's per-account DB file, then drops the now-empty shared table. This is the last bit of per-account state that hadn't migrated yet, and it's blocking a clean re-merge of master.

## Why now

Master's PR #804 (`feat: ignore blocked authors in unread badges`) added a `count_visible_unread_for_group` query that joins `aggregated_messages` (per-account post-Phase 18d) with `mute_list` (shared). That cross-DB subquery can't run on arch-refactor — it fails with `no such table: mute_list` against the per-account pool.

Rather than bridge with `ATTACH DATABASE`, this moves the table to where it logically belongs. After this lands, the next master merge brings master's signature changes through cleanly because both tables now live in the same DB.

## What changed

**Migrations**

- `m0042_move_mute_list` (LocalMigration, v42) creates per-account `mute_list` and copies rows from shared filtered to the owning account. Per-row `rows_affected()` accounting emits `tracing::warn!` on any silently-skipped constraint violations so corrupt source rows leave a diagnostic trail.
- `m0043_drop_shared_mute_list` (GlobalMigration, v43) drops the shared table and its account-scoped index. Runs after every account has completed v42, in the same boot.
- `account_pubkey` column dropped — redundant once the table is per-account. UNIQUE collapses from `(account_pubkey, muted_pubkey)` to `muted_pubkey`.
- Schema baked into `fresh_account_schema.sql` so future bootstrap rebaselines pick it up.

**DAO (`database/mute_list.rs`)**

- `MuteListEntry` no longer carries `account_pubkey`.
- All methods take `&AccountDatabase` instead of `&Database` and drop the `account_pubkey` parameter.
- `find_by_account` → `find_all`; `find_by_account_and_target` → `find_by_muted_pubkey` (matches column-name suffix convention used across other DAOs).
- `exists()` uses `SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 ...)` for short-circuit boolean semantics.

**Session (`session/mute_list.rs`)**

- `db()` returns `&AccountDatabase`.
- `account_relay_urls()` reaches into `&shared.database` directly for `Account` / `User` / `Relay` reads (those tables stay shared).
- `unblock_user` rollback path: explicit `match` with `tracing::debug!` when the entry vanishes between exists-check and read, instead of a silent `unwrap_or(true)`.

**Docs**

- `AccountDatabase` doc comment now lists `mute_list` alongside the other per-account tables.

## Migration safety

- Existing accounts: rows copy from `shared.mute_list WHERE account_pubkey = ?` into the per-account file before v43 drops shared.
- Fresh accounts: bootstrap creates the table from `fresh_account_schema.sql`; m0042's `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` is a no-op; data copy hits empty shared; m0043 drops the empty shared table.
- Idempotency: each migration runs in its own transaction; `INSERT OR IGNORE` makes re-runs safe; `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS` is idempotent.
- Corrupt source rows (CHECK violations on hex format) are silently skipped rather than aborting startup — a `tracing::warn!` records the count, and `migration_silently_skips_invalid_pubkey_rows` test pins this contract.
- Ordering across kinds: the migrator processes a unified version timeline, so all per-account v42 instances complete before the v43 global drop runs.

## Downstream impact

`MuteListEntry` is publicly re-exported via `lib.rs:72`. The `marmot-protocol/whitenoise` Flutter app's bridge layer at `whitenoise/rust/src/api/mute_list.rs` reads `e.account_pubkey.to_hex()` (line 20) plus a unit test that constructs the struct directly. The released app pins whitenoise-rs by git rev so it isn't retroactively broken — but the next rev bump on the Flutter side requires:

- Drop `account_pubkey: String` field from the bridge `MuteListEntry` struct
- Drop `account_pubkey: e.account_pubkey.to_hex()` from the `From` impl
- Update the `WhitenoiseEntry { ... }` literals in the two unit tests
- Run `flutter_rust_bridge_codegen generate` + `dart run build_runner build`

No Dart consumers of `accountPubkey` exist outside the auto-generated bridge code, so the Flutter app side is ~8 lines of Rust + a regen.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Companion PR on `marmot-protocol/whitenoise` that lands together with the eventual arch-refactor → master merge (drops `account_pubkey` from the bridge struct, regen).

## Test plan

- [x] `just precommit-quick` passes — fmt, docs, clippy, dead_code, all unit tests
- [x] m0042 tests: account-scoped copy, empty source, missing shared table, silent skip on invalid hex
- [x] m0043 tests: drops table when present, idempotent when absent
- [x] DAO tests: insert/exists/delete/find_all/find_by_muted_pubkey/sync_from_event with the new schema
- [x] Session tests: block/unblock/sync_and_emit go through the per-account DB

---

Overall this is a solid, well-structured migration. The ordering guarantees are correctly handled by the unified timeline, edge cases are covered, and the test suite is comprehensive. A few observations below.

### Migrations

**m0042 (`move_mute_list.rs`)**

The approach is correct: `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` first (no-op for fresh accounts that already have the table from `fresh_account_schema.sql`), then a filtered copy from shared. The `INSERT OR IGNORE` + `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS` combination ensures idempotency.

One subtle correctness point: the read from `global_db` is not inside the local transaction (line 69–76). The `tx` wraps only the local writes. This is safe here because the shared table is only dropped in m0043, after m0042 completes across all accounts — but if the migration ever needed to treat the read+write as atomic, this would need attention.

The `rows.len() as u64` cast on line 78 is unnecessary — the format string accepts `usize` directly. Minor nit.

**m0043 (`drop_shared_mute_list.rs`)**

Clean and minimal. `DROP INDEX IF EXISTS` before `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS` is the right order. Both tests (`drops_table_when_present`, `idempotent_when_table_absent`) cover the essential paths.

**`fresh_account_schema.sql`**

The added schema at the bottom is byte-for-byte consistent with the inline DDL in m0042. This is important — the comment in `create_test_db()` (database/mute_list.rs:196) explicitly calls out the need to keep these aligned:
> "Schema must stay byte-for-byte aligned with `m0042_move_mute_list.rs` so test/prod don't drift."

It does stay aligned. Good.

**No index needed on `muted_pubkey`**: the `UNIQUE` constraint on `muted_pubkey` creates an implicit B-tree index in SQLite. Lookups in `find_by_muted_pubkey` and `exists` are covered. ✓

### DAO (`database/mute_list.rs`)

The `LocalRow` → `MuteListEntry` two-layer pattern with a custom `FromRow` that parses `PublicKey` at decode time is clean. Errors map to `sqlx::Error::ColumnDecode`, which propagates correctly up to `DatabaseError`.

**`exists` micro-nit** (line 140): `COUNT(*)` works but `EXISTS(SELECT 1 ...)` would short-circuit earlier. For a small table this doesn't matter, but it's more idiomatic for a boolean check:
```rust
// current
sqlx::query_as("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM mute_list WHERE muted_pubkey = ?")
// alternative
sqlx::query_scalar("SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM mute_list WHERE muted_pubkey = ?)")
```
[Fix this →](https://claude.ai/code?q=In%20src%2Fwhitenoise%2Fdatabase%2Fmute_list.rs%20around%20line%20140%2C%20the%20exists()%20method%20uses%20COUNT(*)%20but%20should%20use%20SELECT%20EXISTS(SELECT%201%20...)%20for%20a%20proper%20boolean%20short-circuit%20query.%20Branch%3A%20feat%2Fmute-list-per-account&repo=marmot-protocol/whitenoise-rs)

**`sync_from_event` timestamps** (line 174): all synced entries get `Utc::now().timestamp_millis()` as `created_at`, discarding any temporal information from the event. This matches the behavior of the `insert` path and is consistent — NIP-51 doesn't carry per-mute timestamps in the event payload, so there's nothing to preserve. Acceptable.

**Duplicate handling in `sync_from_event`**: the comment at line 162–166 explains that when the same pubkey appears in both public and private sections, the first occurrence (public tag) wins. This is documented and tested. ✓

### Session (`session/mute_list.rs`)

**`account_relay_urls`** (line 375–397): cleanly bridges the per-account/shared boundary. `Account`, `User`, and `Relay` reads go through `&self.session.shared.database` while mute list reads go through `self.db()` → `&session.account_db`. The boundary is correctly maintained.

**Rollback pattern in `block_user`/`unblock_user`**: the manual application-level rollback (re-insert or re-delete on publish failure) is correct given that the operation spans DB and network. Worth noting: if the rollback itself fails (logged as a warning), the local DB is left inconsistent with the relay state. A subsequent relay sync will repair this. The PR description flags this as an optional follow-up for better observability. The current behavior is acceptable — it's the same tradeoff as the pre-refactor code had.

**`find_by_muted_pubkey` in `unblock_user`** (line 115): calling this right before `delete` means there's a brief window between the existence check and the read where another coroutine could theoretically delete the entry. Given the single-account, single-writer nature of the per-account DB, this is not a real risk in practice.

### Event Handler (`handle_mute_list.rs`)

Foreign author check first — good. `parse_mute_list_entries` returning `None` on decrypt failure prevents cache wipe from a bad event. Tests cover foreign author, own-event public sync, and bad-content no-op. ✓

### `mute_list.rs` (Whitenoise layer)

All four public methods correctly carry `#[deprecated]` with migration hints. The test module exercises the deprecated API via `#[allow(deprecated)]` — standard pattern. ✓

### Downstream break (acknowledged)

The `MuteListEntry` public struct loses `account_pubkey`. The PR description has a clear action plan for the Flutter bridge side (~8 lines + regen). Since the Flutter app pins by git rev, no existing install is broken. The companion PR is the right follow-up.

---

### Summary

| Area | Assessment |
|------|-----------|
| Migration ordering (v42 local before v43 global) | ✓ Guaranteed by unified timeline |
| Data isolation (per-account copy) | ✓ `WHERE account_pubkey = ?` + test |
| Fresh account path | ✓ CREATE IF NOT EXISTS + empty copy |
| Idempotency | ✓ `INSERT OR IGNORE`, `DROP IF EXISTS` |
| Corrupt row handling | ✓ Silently skipped, contract pinned by test |
| DAO API cleanliness | ✓ No `account_pubkey` threading |
| Test coverage | ✓ 4 migration, 6+ DAO, session, event handler |
| Public API break | ⚠ Acknowledged in PR, companion Flutter PR planned |
| Observability on rollback failure | ⚠ Logged at warn, noted as follow-up |

**Minor items (non-blocking):**
- `exists()` could use `SELECT EXISTS(...)` instead of `COUNT(*)`
- `rows.len() as u64` → `rows.len()` (no cast needed)
- Debug/trace log on silently-skipped corrupt rows (mentioned as optional follow-up)

The PR is in good shape. The migration safety analysis in the PR description is accurate and the implementation matches it.

issue.title: Linux headless/container startup fails when Secret Service keyring is unavailable
issue.body:
## Description
When running Whitenoise in a headless Linux/container environment, the daemon fails during startup because the Linux keyring backend requires a Secret Service provider and D-Bus session.

## Error

Error: Whitenoise(SecretsStore(KeyringUnavailable("Failed to create Linux Secret Service credential store: Platform failure: no secret service provider or dbus session found")))

## Environment

- Linux
- Docker / Docker Compose
- Headless runtime, no desktop session
- No DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS
- No GNOME Keyring / KWallet / Secret Service provider running

## Expected behavior

Whitenoise should be able to run in headless/server/container environments, or provide a documented supported key-store option for these environments.

## Actual behavior

Startup fails before the daemon can run because Secret Service initialization fails.

## Why this matters

Secret Service is generally available in desktop Linux sessions, but often absent in:

- Docker containers
- minimal VMs
- servers started over SSH
- systemd services without a user session bus
- CI/headless environments

This makes the current Linux default unsuitable for many daemon deployments.

## Possible fixes

A few options that would make this work better:

- Support an explicit file-backed key store for headless/container deployments.
- Support configuration via env var or CLI flag, for example WHITENOISE_KEYRING_BACKEND=file.
- Fall back to a non-Secret-Service backend when no D-Bus session is available.
- Document the Secret Service/D-Bus requirement and provide a supported headless setup.

In my Docker Compose setup, I worked around this by building with keyring-core’s sample feature and configuring a file-backed store persisted in the same Docker volume as the Whitenoise data directory. That avoids the need for Secret Service/D-Bus inside the
  container.

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_ | _🏗️ Heavy lift_

**Validate the account/group pair before creating a stream.**

This method currently succeeds for any `(account_pubkey, group_id)` and eagerly allocates a stream entry, so a typoed or arbitrary pair turns into a dead subscription instead of a fast `GroupNotFound`-style failure. Because this API is now public, callers can also create unbounded orphaned streams by probing random keys.

`subscribe_to_group_messages` already guards the same invariant before subscribing; this API should do the same and return a `Result`.

<details>
<summary>Suggested direction</summary>

```diff
-    pub fn subscribe_to_group_state(
+    pub async fn subscribe_to_group_state(
         &self,
         account_pubkey: &PublicKey,
         group_id: &mdk_core::prelude::GroupId,
-    ) -> group_state_streaming::GroupStateSubscription {
-        group_state_streaming::GroupStateSubscription {
+    ) -> Result<group_state_streaming::GroupStateSubscription> {
+        AccountGroup::chat_cleared_at_ms(account_pubkey, group_id, &self.database).await?;
+
+        Ok(group_state_streaming::GroupStateSubscription {
             updates: self
                 .group_state_stream_manager
                 .subscribe(account_pubkey, group_id),
-        }
+        })
     }
```
</details>

In this whitenoise flutter PR https://github.com/marmot-protocol/whitenoise/pull/537 a notice was added when the user was removed from a group. This is done in a very inefficient way opening the chat list stream to request all chats to then filter by id.  It is doing so because in that stream the type ChatSummary already has that info, There is no need to request all chats for this


# Solution
- I would like to pass the rust side my group id and my account id  and get if I was removed or if I left a group. 
- 💡  What I imagine is having a method to get the chat summary by group and account id would be enough... and I think it would be cleaner for flutter side, that single method would avoid us calling (get_group + group_members + get_group_image_path)
- But I'm open to any other solutions proposed that the achieve this goal

issue.title: Blocking users doesn't prevent from receiving messages from them
issue.body:
**Describe the bug**
After blocking a user (calling `.block_user`) , chat list stream and chat stream still send me events of new messages, when I would expect that those message stop arriving. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior in the whitenoise app:
1. Go to chat list
2. Enter a dm chat of a chat you have acces from other devices
3. Block the user
4. GO back to chat list
5. From the other device, send a message to the user who blocked you
6. 🐛 Check that you still receive the message in the chat list 
7. Enter the chat screen
8. From the other device, send another message to the user who blocked you
9. 🐛 Check that you still receive the message in the chat screen

**Expected behavior**
I would expect to stop receiving messages in chat list and chat screen from a blocked user

**Screenshots**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dbae9f74-18d7-43c7-9a75-d450a7e2f149

**Smartphone (please complete the following information):**
 - Device: iPhone 11
